headline: Approved new historic house plaques and voted on CPC-funded preservation projects
summary: The Historical Commission approved the June 29, 2026 meeting minutes and six new historic house plaque applications. It reviewed updates on the Demolition Delay Ordinance, MACRIS records, tercentenary markers, preservation restrictions, and the Lanesville/Lane's Cove National Registry District application. It also voted to approve CPC funding for the Maritime Gloucester marine railway project and agreed to write a letter supporting the Lanes Cove plaque project.
decisions: Approved the June 29, 2026 meeting minutes, all in favor.
Approved six new historic house plaque applications (281 East Main St, 5 Wiley St, 28 Friend St, 11 Pirates Lane/NSAA, 34-36 Summer St, 1206 Washington St), all in favor.
Approved CPC funding for Maritime Gloucester's Burnham Marine Railways project, all in favor.
Approved writing a letter in support of the Lanes Cove Plaque project, all in favor.

CPC UPDATE (Maggie)  
● Review CPC-mandated qualification criteria for CPC-funded historic projects 
o Former criteria was inclusion in MACRIS 
o New criteria: One or more of these designations -  Local Historic District, Local Landmark, MA 
Archaeo/Historic Landmark, National Historic Landmark, Preservation Restriction OR 
applicant needs to attend a GHC meeting to verify historic significance 
● Brief update on 10 applicants requesting historic funding 
o Hammond Castle – Replacing severely deteriorated windows on the ocean-facing side of the 
castle with historically accurate replicas fabricated by the same company that fabricated the 
original windows when the castle was built nearly 100 years ago (Hope’s Windows, Inc).   
o Schooner Adventure – Replace planking and top timbers and side rail.  They have already 
purchased (some with prior CPC funds) the wood needed and it will be available and properly 
dried and seasoned in advance of the work to be done.  They are very conscious, 
knowledgeable, and experienced about their historic asset and its appropriate treatment. 
o UU Cemetery – Conservation of gravestones.  “This work will be done by a conservation 
professional and carried out in accordance with the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for 
the Treatment of Historic Properties and its treatment for rehabilitation.” (from their 
application)
o Maritime Gloucester – Rehabilitation of the marine railway. They will be replacing chain links 
and other specialized pieces of equipment.  It will be managed and overseen by qualified 
professionals. 
VOTE on Burnham Marine Railways: Bob makes a motion, Susan seconds, all in favor 
o North Shore Arts – Looking to replace, on the second floor, six windows and add a window 
where there is now a door, historic plaque application approved tonight. 
o Saunders House Reading Room – Adding an accessible bathroom, addressing structural 
ceiling issues and replacing outdated ceiling tiles with historically appropriate plaster, 
reconstructing sub-flooring to make it level with the adjacent Matz Gallery, removing non-
historic wall shelving and cabinets and prepping and repainting walls. Some of this work is 
within the historical portion of the building.  The budget for the project was developed from 
cost estimates prepared by a contractor and through the Spencer Preservation Group 
o RNCC – The RNCC currently requires significant restoration to include floor, front entry, and 
window frames due to years of continuous public use and challenging weather conditions. 
The front gateway to Rocky Neck Art Colony’s 1877 Cultural Center is the first impression 
visitors receive, reflecting the care, vitality and historical significance of this beloved cultural 
landmark. Restoring the Cultural Center’s original historic window sashes preserves a 
defining architectural feature of the building while maintaining its historic integrity without 
replacing the windows. Confirmation of the preservation specialists' involvement is needed. 
o Gloucester Stage – The funds are to be used for repointing brickwork, as the mortar has 
deteriorated in many areas due to the proximity to saltwater.  It has been over 40 years since 
the building was last repointed. An expert mason has assessed the building and identified 
visible damage, although more may be found once the cracks are opened. Repairs could 
involve simple mortar work or may require replacing several courses of brick.  One large wall 
is completely obscured by decades of ivy and vine growth and needs further examination. 
o Wellspring House – The original clapboard siding of this 1709 structure has deteriorated 
significantly and is in need of replacement and repair, along with rot repair and restoration of 
period trim and decorative corner pieces. Maggie will obtain more information about the 
experience of Heirloom Builders and their specific plans for this building. 
o Manship – The larger project is the renovation of the Ox Barn complex, the former studio and 
exhibition space used by Paul Manship.  As the first phase of a larger campus revitalization 
effort, this phase will restore the heart of the Manship landscape – the West Arbor.  It is 
currently not able to be used due to a safety issue.  It will be recreated to Paul Manship’s 
specifications thereby expanding opportunities for artists and the public to use and enjoy the 
space. MARS will use the detailed project cost estimate prepared by Applewood Enterprises 
as well as recent Historic Structure Reports to engage appropriately qualified contractors 
with experience in historic renovation projects.

LANESVILLE/Lane’s Cove NATIONAL REGISTRY DISTRICT APPLICATION (Ralph) 
● First step: Letter created by Ralph and emailed 8/20/26 to MHC seeking approval for a nomination;            
Reply from Ben Haley/Nat Reg Director at MHC 8/24/26: 
“Evaluations for National Register eligibility are undertaken by reviewing recent Inventory form documentation. 
In the case of Certified Local Governments like Gloucester, the historical commission of that 
municipality undertakes the first evaluation and provides its opinion on a specific form and then provides 
that to us along with whatever Inventory form(s) were u sed for the evaluation. The MHC then reviews the 
material and concurs, disagrees, or requests additional information. l have attached the CLG NR opinion 
form. I see the 2016 Inventory form for Lanesville. As a ten -year-old form for a couple dozen properties, that 
can form the basis for an evaluation, but since quite a lot can change in ten years, the existing conditions there 
will need to be reviewed by someone (the historical commission, a consultant) and updated on Inventory 
Continuation Sheets (the template for that can be found here: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/mhc/mhc-
forms.htm. This new documentation must include new photography and any information on demolitions, new 
construction, and additions/major alterations to previously documented resources. If you wish to propose a 
smaller area, I recommend that the commission create or fund the creation of an Area form specifically 
for this smaller area. Please note, however, that National Register district boundaries are not chosen based 
on potential property owner support. They are determined by the extent of historic thematic/functional 
relationships. A property related to one or more themes for a prop osed district cannot be omitted because an 
owner objects to inclusion. I hope this is helpful.” 
• Due to concerns and uncertainty in obtaining funding, Ralph volunteered to take a first pass at 
completing the form for the smaller area of Lanes Cove, landing, Fish Shack, cemetery + others
